description: WALK THE WHOLE PURCHASE OF AN x402 ENDPOINT WITHOUT PAYING, in the order a buyer actually asks the questions, stopping at the first one that objects. Every other tool here answers ONE question about one subject; the losses live between them. Five steps: is the endpoint there, what does it charge RIGHT NOW, does the seller’s own catalogue entry agree with what it just said, does the record say anything against paying that payee under a published policy, and — the step that only exists because this is a rehearsal — is the price still the one the decision was made on, re-read a moment later. A quote that moved between the decision and the signature would authorise something nobody decided on. THE VERDICT HAS THREE STATES AND cannot-tell IS NOT would-proceed: an unanswered question is never rounded up to a passed one. `quotedRaw` is what the endpoint said, in the asset’s smallest unit, and `quotedUsd` is NULL unless the catalogue carries both halves of the same token’s pair to scale it — nothing in a payment-requirements document names the decimals, and a figure scaled by a guessed exponent is a hundred-fold error waiting to be quoted. We knock only on endpoints already in the x402 catalogue we read, at most one live handshake a minute per resource, because fetching a URL because a request named it would make us a prober-for-hire pointed at somebody else’s host. Nothing is signed and nothing is spent. FREE.

policy.description: A policy version or slug to decide under. Defaults to conservative-v1.

resource.description: The http(s) endpoint to rehearse buying. It must be one the x402 catalogue already holds; `list_x402_endpoints` finds it.

name: test_purchase

cannotSee.description: What no rehearsal establishes however well it goes.

decidedAt.description: The id of the step that stopped it, so a caller acts on a step rather than parsing a sentence.

live.description: Whether the handshake happened just now or is the stored reading from within the last minute. A stored reading is a weaker claim and this says which it is.

network.description: The chain the endpoint asked to be paid on, as it stated it, usually CAIP-2.

payee.description: The address the ENDPOINT named in its handshake, which is not always the one its listing names. That disagreement is step three.

quotedRaw.description: What it asked for, in the asset’s smallest unit. Always the number the endpoint actually said.

quotedUsd.description: The same amount in dollars, NULL where we could not scale it from the catalogue’s own pair.

rehearsed.description: False where the endpoint is not in the catalogue, with `says` explaining that we do not fetch a URL because a request named it.

resource.description: The endpoint this is about, read back.

says.description: The verdict in one sentence: where a careful buyer stops and why, or what could not be answered. An unanswered question is named rather than passed over.

steps.description: One per question, in the order a buyer asks them. Each carries `asks` in a person’s words, `state`, `stops` and `says`.

verdict.description: `would-proceed`, `would-stop` or `cannot-tell`. The third is NOT the first.

title: Test purchase, without paying
